clue.text: Ex-PM keeps appealing to the top people in the country

indicators.note: a thing that keeps something holds it inside, so the ex-premier's name wraps the other piece

parts.note: David Cameron, former British Prime Minister
U is the old label for upper-class usage, what appeals to the top people

explanation.surface: A former prime minister still courts the elite of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French spelling of Cameroon, the central African country.

clue.text: Travelling fans late — coaches not moving here?

indicators.note: fans who are travelling are on the move, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Supporters running late on the way to a match fret that their coaches are stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: On British motorways buses and coaches may not use the outermost lane, hence the question mark: coaches do not move there.
explanation.definitionFit: UK rules bar coaches from the outside overtaking lane of a motorway, so it is where coaches do not travel.

clue.text: In a row nothing upset listener

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: In an argument, a hearer is not at all upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Things arranged in a straight line, one after another, are set out in a row.

clue.text: Hearing US style, unpleasant modern form of our language

indicators.note: the style heard is ugly and mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that a grating American-influenced accent is spoiling British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name given to the south-eastern accent spreading from the Thames region, a recent variety of the native tongue.

clue.text: Cleric, very big fool, set up religious festival

indicators.note: in a down clue setting up raises the pieces so they read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
OS is the size label for outsize
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a huge idiot organise a holy celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the whole chain REVOSSAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish spring festival marking the Exodus from Egypt is a religious feast.

clue.text: I tire and can go funny — caused by medical treatment?

indicators.note: something funny is odd or out of order, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A patient complains that tiredness and strange bowels might be side effects of their medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical adjective describes illness brought on by a doctor's own intervention or drugs.

clue.text: Abandon rail transport, losing heart with delay

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for leaving a train goes missing

parts.note: to detrain is to get off a train

explanation.surface: Passengers get off the train in despair at the hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone back or hold them up is to hinder their progress.

clue.text: Boy and I in children's game knocked over champions

indicators.note: the boy and I sit inside the game's name
something knocked over lies the other way, so the game's name runs backwards

parts.note: Snap is a children's card game
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy and the speaker upset a game of cards among youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns SNAP into PANS, which then holds LAD and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The paladins were Charlemagne's knights, so the word means heroic defenders of a cause.

clue.text: Stunned in the morning by Observer crossword

parts.note: a.m. marks the morning hours
Azed is the long-running barred crossword in the Observer newspaper

explanation.surface: A solver is left reeling after tackling a hard weekend puzzle over breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astonished or astounded is being left stunned with surprise.

clue.text: Oatmeal exceptionally fine in dish

indicators.note: taken as out of the ordinary, it shows the letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Praise for a bowl of porridge that is unusually good.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat baked in a tin shape is a familiar main course.

clue.text: Rider in crusade flanked by monarch and Scotsman

indicators.note: the crusade has the two letters for the monarch on either side of it

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a quest is a crusade or mission
Ian is a typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: A knight on a holy war rides between a king and a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseman or horsewoman is a rider.

clue.text: Finisher, not starter? That's very good!

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for something that finishes is dropped

parts.note: a stopper brings things to an end

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who finishes but does not start, as a cricket or relay quip.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is informal British for an excellent thing or person, something that tops the rest.

clue.text: Moving up in trade gaining pounds, showing business sense?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters gain one more at their end
the letters are moving about into a new order

parts.note: L stands for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: Rising in commerce and making money shows a good head for business.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful and wise with money is a kind of commercial good judgment.

clue.text: It's destructive, showing anger about traditional Bible

indicators.note: the angry word goes round the Bible version

parts.note: raging means furiously angry
AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible

explanation.surface: Fury over an old scripture does damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying waste and devastating is destructive behaviour.

clue.text: Grow weak, left out in pain

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out

parts.note: to languish is to weaken and fade

explanation.surface: A patient left alone wastes away in suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe mental or physical suffering is acute pain.

clue.text: Cheats in society, endlessly calm

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for still air is cut off

parts.note: windless weather is calm

explanation.surface: Fraudsters thrive in a world that is forever untroubled.
explanation.definitionFit: To defraud or con someone is to cheat them.

clue.text: There's little right in fiddle creating dispute

indicators.note: the short form of right goes inside the fiddle

parts.note: to wangle is to fiddle or wheedle something
R is the abbreviated form of right

explanation.surface: A small swindle sparks a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A long noisy argument is a dispute.

clue.text: City road goes round country to the north

indicators.note: the road surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
USA, the United States
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A city's road encircles the nation northward.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Swiss city on Lake Geneva, home of the Olympic committee.

clue.text: See 4
Laissez-faire type? Not sailor from African country

indicators.note: the sailor is not there, so his letters are dropped

parts.note: a libertarian favours minimal state interference
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A free-market thinker, not a seaman, hails from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Liberia describes a person or thing from that West African state.

clue.text: One unpleasant person outside work, one with fourteen members

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the nasty person sits outside the work

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A nasty colleague hangs about the office, as if with seven pairs of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlice and their crustacean relatives typically have seven pairs of legs, fourteen limbs.

clue.text: Activity on rugby field trapping a bone

indicators.note: the rugby set piece traps the a inside it

parts.note: a scrum is the rugby set piece where the forwards bind and push

explanation.surface: A rugby scrum catches someone's bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular bone at the base of the spine is part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Channel links Home Counties to "abroad"

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
being abroad is being away

explanation.surface: A sea crossing connects the area around London to foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigable waterway such as a ship canal is a channel for vessels.

clue.text: Sausage roll made at Barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A sausage roll produced in Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a large Italian cured pork sausage from Bologna.

clue.text: See 10
See 2
Troublesome kid eating egg with a little bit of extra salt

indicators.note: the kid eats the egg, taking it inside

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
O looks like an egg

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A naughty child eats an egg with too much salt sprinkled on.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical salt of boric acid is a kind of salt.

clue.text: Breeding of man covered in grass

indicators.note: the chessman is covered by the informer's word

parts.note: to grass is to inform, to sing to the police
a pawn is a chess man

explanation.surface: Reproduction of a man lying hidden in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing eggs or offspring in quantity, as fish do, is breeding.
